title: Feralas
body: Feralas is a vast, rain-soaked forest in southwestern Kalimdor, green and wild beside the dry lands that surround it. Long ago the night elves built here, and their ruins lie everywhere beneath the canopy, above all the broken city of Eldre'Thalas, now called Dire Maul. Today the Gordunni ogres are the strongest power in the forest, and the land withers wherever they settle. On Sardor Isle, off the western shore, General Shandris Feathermoon holds Feathermoon Stronghold for the Alliance, the tauren of Camp Mojache keep the Horde's watch in the east, and the small way-station of Thalanaar stands on the border with the Thousand Needles. Neither side has the forest to itself. Woodpaw gnolls, Grimtotem tauren, Northspring harpies and Hatecrest naga each claim a share, the insect hive of the Zukk'ash festers in the southeast, and in the far north the great tree called the Dream Bough rises from an island in Jademir Lake, guarded by the green dragons of the Emerald Dream.

title: Thalanaar
body: Thalanaar is a small night elf way-station on the eastern edge of Feralas, where the forest gives way to the dry canyons of the Thousand Needles. It offers little more than a hippogryph roost, a pair of merchants and a trainer of tribal leatherworking, yet it matters more than its size suggests. The druid Falfindel Waywarder keeps his post here, and couriers from Feathermoon Stronghold cross the whole breadth of Feralas to bring him supplies. Travelers remark on how abruptly the green forest ends at this border. One scholar who studies the barren lands beyond is sure that strange magic was at work when that happened.

title: Camp Mojache
body: Camp Mojache is the Horde's foothold in Feralas, a tauren camp of hide tents built astride a swift stream above Wildwind Lake. Braves guard its paths, and it has an inn, a wind rider roost and trainers of many crafts. It is a meeting place as much as a village. The elder Talo Thornhoof tells his stories here, the troll Witch Doctor Uzer'i studies the spirits of beasts, the warrior Rok Orhan leads the fight against the ogres, and Krueg Skullsplitter has come on an errand from Orgrimmar. Its neighbors give it little peace. Woodpaw gnolls press up from the south with growing fury, and the Gordunni hold the river valley to the north.

title: Lariss Pavilion
body: North of Camp Mojache stands Lariss Pavilion, a large open-air hall raised in the old night elf style. Its strangest tenant is Azj'Tordin, a Highborne who slipped out of Dire Maul and the grip of its mad prince. He lingers here among the old stones, savoring the freedom for which he gave up his immortality, though he fled the city in such haste that he was robbed on the way. A door at the foot of the pavilion is said to lead back into the old city.

title: Gordunni Outpost
body: Following the river north from Camp Mojache leads to the Gordunni Outpost, a camp of the ogres who dominate Feralas. Ogres, brutes and ogre magi crowd it, and the land around them bears the scars of their presence. They guard more than their tents. The Gordunni bury a mineral called Gordunni cobalt in the earth here, betrayed only by its blue glow, and a goblin prospector newly arrived at Camp Mojache wants it dug up, sure it will fetch a pretty price. Soiled scrolls lie about the camp as well, and one of them seems to depict some sort of meeting or ceremony of the ogres, a puzzle that Rok Orhan of Camp Mojache would dearly like to see solved.

title: Woodpaw Hills
body: South of Camp Mojache, the wooded hills belong to the Woodpaw gnolls, who keep a den deep among them. Mystics, reavers, trappers and brutes fill their camps, and their leaders call themselves Alphas. Their raids on the tauren have grown more frequent and more savage, almost as if the gnolls were desperate, and Camp Mojache wonders what has driven them into such a frenzy. Like all gnolls they keep what they scavenge and fight over it. A rare treant, Gnarl Leafbrother, is sometimes seen among the hills.

title: The Writhing Deep
body: Beyond the Woodpaw camps in southeastern Feralas, the earth is broken into the twisted mounds and tunnels of the Writhing Deep, a hive of the insects known here as the Zukk'ash. Workers, wasps, stingers and tunnelers swarm over its slopes, and even the ore in its veins comes smeared with ooze. Among them roams Stinglasher, far larger than its kin and wrapped in an aura the others lack.

title: Grimtotem Compound
body: East of Dire Maul, the Grimtotem tribe has raised a compound of tents in the Feralas woods, guarded by raiders, shamans and naturalists. These tauren are hostile to every outsider, and their work here is dark. In a bamboo pen nearby they keep captured sprite darters, the faerie dragons of the forest, for purposes no one has learned. Two night elves, Kindal Moonweaver and the priestess Jer'kai, keep watch over the camp from a rise above it. The Horde has taken notice too: in Orgrimmar, Belgrom Rockmaul has put a bounty on the clan's horns.

title: Dire Maul
body: In the heart of Feralas rise the broken walls of Eldre'Thalas, a city of Queen Azshara's Highborne, its great halls now called Dire Maul. The Queen is long gone, and the Shen'dralar who linger within have been marred by the madness of their Prince Tortheldrin. Gordok ogres hold the grounds outside, their hyenas prowling among the fallen stones, and in an arena within the walls, the Maul, ogre champions brawl while spectators such as Griniblix cheer them on. Deeper in, the wings hold satyrs, a rogue blood elf mage and perhaps the last refuge of a lost elven master.

title: The High Wilderness
body: The High Wilderness spreads across the uplands of southern Feralas, a broad country of forest glades and broken ground. Groddoc apes, ironfur bears and longtooth howlers roam it, Frayfeather hippogryphs wheel over its clearings, and Feral Scar yetis prowl its slopes. This was once night elf land, and its abandoned, ruined buildings still stand. The Gordunni ogres have claimed them, and where they dwell the trees wither and the ground is desecrated. The Feathermoon scholar Troyas Moonbreeze often comes here alone to study the ruins, much to the worry of Angelas Moonbreeze.

title: Ruins of Isildien
body: Deep in the High Wilderness lie the Ruins of Isildien, the remains of a large night elf city destroyed long ages ago. A broad stair climbs to a round hall that may once have been a temple. The Gordunni have made the ruins their stronghold, and here gather their mightiest: battlemasters, warlords, warlocks, maulers and the mage-lords of the tribe. Their magic seems to wreak havoc on the very ground they stand on. Frayfeather hippogryphs still nest at the edges of the ruins, and an old bear called Old Grizzlegut is known to wander nearby.

title: Feral Scar Vale
body: Feral Scar Vale is a valley of yetis in southern Feralas, just inland of the Forgotten Coast. Its yetis grow hides so thick that leatherworkers in both Feathermoon Stronghold and Camp Mojache prize them, claiming that properly treated they are as strong as iron. A rare brute called Bloodroar the Stalker hunts the vale. In a cave nearby lies a stranger find: OOX-22/FE, a gnomish homing robot that looks rather like a chicken. It crashed here, and its maker in Booty Bay calls for someone to carry a beacon to it and escort it safely to the road.

title: Frayfeather Highlands
body: In the far south of Feralas, the Frayfeather Highlands are home to great flocks of wild hippogryphs: stagwings, skystormers and the proud patriarchs that lead them. Hippogryphs have been loyal companions to the night elves for many years, and their eggs can be found in nests across these heights. That loyalty has drawn unwelcome attention, for Witch Doctor Uzer'i of Camp Mojache covets the steadfast spirits of these birds for his muisek magic. The greatest of the flock, a hippogryph known as Antilus the Soarer, is seldom seen.

title: The Twin Colossals
body: Two immense peaks of rock tower over northwestern Feralas, the highest points in the land, and the road to Desolace runs between them. Mountain giants stride across the rocky ground at their feet, and Groddoc thunderers, ironfur patriarchs and rabid longtooths make every path dangerous. A few odd souls camp here. Marli Wishrunner can send a traveler to the top of a colossal, though only one way, and Kalin Windflight waits at the summit selling wings for the trip down. The gentle giant Rockbiter keeps a camp south of the Ruins of Ravenwind, and Gregan Brewspewer, a student of herbs who is hard to track down, keeps a camp out in these wilds.

title: Ruins of Ravenwind
body: West of the Dream Bough lie the Ruins of Ravenwind, remains of an ancient night elf city now overrun by the Northspring harpies. Their queen, Edana Hatetalon, is said to have a heart of crystal, empty of all but hatred, and she comes when a harpy horn is sounded by the Hatetalon stones in the northern ruins. Older magic lingers among the stones. Four flames named Samha, Imbel, Byltan and Lahassa still burn there, and the Equinex Monolith stands silent nearby, keeping whatever it holds. On the eastern edge of the ruins, a gnoll named Miblon Snarltooth stands guard over a patch of evoroot.

title: The Dream Bough
body: In the far north of Feralas, Jademir Lake spreads its quiet waters around an island where a towering tree, the Dream Bough, rises above the forest. It is one of four great trees through which the Emerald Dream touches the waking world; the others stand in Duskwood, the Hinterlands and Ashenvale. The green dragonflight guards it jealously. The dragons Lethlas and Dreamroarer keep watch over the island, and Jademir dragonkin patrol the lake shores and the grounds of Oneiros. Few mortals linger.

title: The Forgotten Coast
body: The Forgotten Coast is the western shore of Feralas, looking out across the water to Sardor Isle. Elementals of brine and sea spray rise from the surf, coast crawl creatures scuttle on the sand, and towering giants of the shore and the deep wade through the shallows. A dock here serves the ferry to Feathermoon Stronghold, and beside it the goblin Zorbin Fandazzle is trying, with growing doubts, to run an engineering shop. Not every boat makes its crossing. The wreck of a row boat lies in the muddy water nearby, its side torn open as if something had tried to snap it in two.

title: Sardor Isle
body: Sardor Isle lies off the Forgotten Coast, a forested island that the night elves of Feathermoon Stronghold have made their own. Beyond the stronghold's walls the island is wild. Coast crawl snapclaws and deepseers swarm its beaches, longtooth runners hunt in its woods, and a rare beast called Diamond Head lurks along its shore. South of the stronghold, the Ruins of Solarsal have fallen to the Hatecrest naga, and the Sentinels fear that the naga mean in time to seize the whole island. The Isle of Dread lies across the water beyond.

title: Feathermoon Stronghold
body: Feathermoon Stronghold is the Alliance bastion of Feralas, a night elf fortress on Sardor Isle reached by ferry from the Forgotten Coast or on hippogryph wings. General Shandris Feathermoon led an expeditionary force here and commands it still, with Feathermoon Sentinels on watch. It is a place of scholars as much as soldiers. Troyas and Angelas Moonbreeze pore over their books on the ruins of Feralas, the priestess Vestia Moonspear is one of the most learned minds to be found anywhere, the druid Quintis Jonespyre keeps a tree house, and a history of the Sentinels and the Long Vigil is kept for visitors. Its defenders watch two foes: the naga to the south and the Horde.

title: Ruins of Solarsal
body: The Ruins of Solarsal, on Sardor Isle south of Feathermoon Stronghold, are far older than any of the night elves' present works. The Sentinels once explored them, found nothing of note and left them in peace. Now the Hatecrest naga have filled them in alarming numbers: warriors, screamers, sirens and wave riders. At the heart of the ruins stands a gazebo that does not belong. It is clearly newer than the stones around it, its sides are engraved with a repeating band of unknown glyphs, and its stone is warm to the touch.

Hatecrest serpent guards, myrmidons and sorceresses hold a deep cave at its northern end, Shalzaru's Lair, the seat of Lord Shalzaru, one of the crueler naga royals. A hidden passage beneath the waves is said to lead to an inner chamber where Lady Szallah dwells. The heart of the island, a valley walled in by cliffs, belongs to beasts deadlier still: the chimaerok, great two-headed hunters, led by the mighty Lord Lakmaeran.

Orphaned when the Burning Legion destroyed her village during the War of the Ancients, she was taken in by Tyrande Whisperwind and grew up at her side, through the Sundering and the long ages of the Sentinels, until she rose to lead them. In Feralas she weighs every move against the safety of her island. She would gladly throw her full strength against the Hatecrest naga, but she will not leave the stronghold open to the Horde.

He has no patience for idle talk and is proud of his people's restraint: the night elves are no warmongers, he says, but they will act to protect their own. When the blood elf mage Lethtendris fled into Dire Maul with a web of stolen magic, it was Latronicus who called for agents to stop her. His wife Vestia is a priestess of the stronghold and one of its most learned scholars, and Latro, as she calls him when she forgets herself, brings her the puzzles he cannot solve.

Curses are his specialty, and he can read the history of an object by touch, a draining art he calls psychometry. His luck at cards is another matter. The stronghold calls him the King of the Bad Beats, and he owes Ginro Hearthkindle for his losses at Kalimdor Hold 'Em.

He ventures alone into the ogre-held High Wilderness, and from the rubble of the south he once pulled a stave that he was sure was more than it seemed, though a colleague in Rut'theran grumbles that he always thinks he has found something important. Angelas worries over him, and quietly asks travelers to thin the Gordunni in his path, begging them not to tell him. She also sends the curious to the goblin Marvon Rivetseeker to learn of the Sunken Temple.

Yet his name is known well beyond Feralas, further than so small a post would suggest.

When she slipped off from him in the ruins to the north, Rockbiter was sick with worry and hardly knew what to do, and he hoped that someone with quicker legs than his would go and look for her.

title: Talo Thornhoof
body: Talo Thornhoof is a tauren elder of Camp Mojache who is always glad to share his stories. In his day he was a seasoned hunter who feared no creature, until Northspring harpies ambushed him in the forest and he barely dragged himself to safety. He was never the same, and the hate still boils in him. He longs for revenge on the harpies and for the crystal heart of their queen, Edana Hatetalon. He still thinks like a hunter: know your enemy, he teaches, and he sends the bold to test the fel-maddened beasts of Felwood. When the blood elf Lethtendris carried her web into Dire Maul, Talo called for help.

The Queen has long since passed, he says, and the works of the Shen'dralar have been marred by the madness of Prince Tortheldrin. He has traded his immortality for freedom and regrets nothing. In the haste of his escape, though, he was robbed. The imp Pusillin made off with his book of incantations and with the key to the once great halls. The key he no longer cares for. body: Zorbin Fandazzle is a goblin engineer who has set up shop beside the dock on the Forgotten Coast against his own better judgment, and now suspects it may be the worst place imaginable. The giants of Feralas are bad for business, so he has built an Ultra-Shrinker, a gnomish shrinking ray improved with superior goblin know-how, and wants someone to try it on them. Then there are the sea elementals of the coast, whose water cores make fine fuel for his device. He insists there was never any danger, pays in coin and loot, and swears that his comrades in the Steamwheedle Cartel will hear of anyone who helps him.

Before his strength failed, Heralath begged the dwarf to carry word to Falfindel Waywarder at Thalanaar: the crone Charlga Razorflank was rousing her minions, and she had to be stopped before her corruption spread. body: Raschal has carried Feathermoon's messages since Shandris Feathermoon brought her expedition to Feralas, and he knows the forest well. About a week ago he set out for Thalanaar, meaning to row down the coast and cross southern Feralas to avoid the Horde camp, and he never arrived. The stronghold's own searches found nothing, and Latronicus Moonspear has had to declare him missing in action. His friend Ginro Hearthkindle would not give up, though every day's search in the wilds brought him back nothing but gnoll teeth and disappointment.

title: Freedom for All Creatures
body: From a rise above the Grimtotem Compound, Kindal Moonweaver and the priestess Jer'kai keep watch on the tauren below. The filthy Grimtotem, as Kindal calls them, are capturing faerie dragons, the sprite darters of the forest, and penning them in a bamboo cage, and neither elf can guess what for. The two are not strong enough to fight their way into the camp alone. Kindal's plan is to carry a cage key into the compound with a helper and some strong friends, throw open the pen and stay beside the darters until they escape with their lives, while Jer'kai keeps her post on the rise.

parts.body: Picking off naturalists, raiders and shamans in the camp below and in the camps to the east, the two elves soon counted their kills in the dozens, and the Grimtotem began hunting them like vipers in turn. Jer'kai wondered whether other tauren frowned on these, since many races have their less kindly cousins.

parts.body: With little to give out in the wilds, Jer'kai had sent her signet ring to High Priestess Tyrande Whisperwind in Darnassus as word that the two of them were well. In the meantime the Moonweavers saved a nest of sprite darter eggs whose mother had died before they reached her. The eggs were close to hatching, and they offered one to their helper as a pet, sending it first to the scholar Quentin at the race tracks of the Shimmering Flats.

parts.body: Quentin found the egg healthy and near maturation, a rare find now that poachers have hunted the darters of Feralas, and sent it on to Agnar Beastamer, the animal handler of Aerie Peak. Agnar had Silvermane stalker flanks gathered for its first meal, but the egg was readier than he thought, and the faerie dragon hatched to bond with the one who had carried it so far.

title: The Stave of Equinex
body: Searching the rubble to the south a few days ago, Troyas Moonbreeze found a stave that looks ordinary, yet he cannot shake the feeling that it is something more. The ruins of Feralas are dangerous, but they have much to tell of what happened here. He and Angelas have pored over their books at Feathermoon Stronghold without finding a word about it, so Troyas has sent for help to a colleague in Darnassus, the lore keeper Daryn Lightwind of Rut'theran Village.
sources: quests 2939, 2940, 2941, 2944, 2943, 2879, 2942 descriptions and reward texts

parts.body: Daryn was unimpressed. Troyas always thinks he has found something important, she grumbled, when anything of value in those ruins was hoarded long ago by the ogres or the harpies. Still, she owned a worn old history of Feralas, and she would lend it for a price: a picture of Gammerita, a giant snapjaw of the Hinterlands, taken with a device that the inventor Curgle Cranklehop built for her in Tanaris.

parts.body: With the book in hand, Troyas dared to hope that his find was the Stave of Equinex, the key to the Equinex Monolith in the Ruins of Ravenwind, west of the Dream Bough. Charged with the essence of the four flames that still burn there, Samha, Imbel, Byltan and Lahassa, it should unlock the monolith and the sacred artifact within.

The stone inside was brought back to Troyas, who, reading on, named it the Morrow Stone. He cannot yet say what it is for, but anything hidden away with such care must be of great significance.

title: War on the Woodpaw
body: To Hadoken Swiftstrider of Camp Mojache, the Woodpaw gnolls are more than a nuisance: they are a constant threat to the camp's very existence. Whether or not they belong in Feralas matters little to him. If the tauren do not strengthen their resolve, he warns, they will find themselves driven out of the whole region, and the gnoll attacks have grown more fevered of late. Hadoken has answered with a bounty on Woodpaw manes, and he suspects that someone or something is driving the gnolls into a frenzy.
sources: quests 2862, 2863, 2902, 2903, 7730, 7731, 7732 descriptions and reward texts

parts.body: In times past the camp had always driven them back, but lately they pushed north far more often and more savagely, almost as if they were desperate. Hadoken's answer was a stroke meant to throw them into chaos: five of their leaders, the Alphas, cut down in swift succession.

parts.body: The Alphas fell, but Hadoken still wanted to know what drove the gnolls, and a battle map taken from their camps told the tale. Most of its arrows pointed south, away from Camp Mojache, and beside them was drawn a great insect with tally marks beneath. The gnolls were fighting on two fronts, and their main strength was spent against a foe to their south.

parts.body: That foe was an insect race, the Zukk'ash of the Writhing Deep. Their swarms were thinned, and the giant Stinglasher, larger than its kin and wrapped in a strange aura, was cut open so that its glands could be studied. Yet nothing short of a full invasion would break the hive, and Hadoken sent all he had learned to Zilzibin Drumlore in the Drag of Orgrimmar, an expert on alien creatures.

parts.body: Zilzibin had been expecting the report. The Zukk'ash, he said, are nothing more than the silithid, an ancient threat that the Horde keeps choosing to ignore. Some think them a mindless nuisance, but they are a far, far worse threat than anything the Alliance could muster.

title: The Ogres of Feralas
body: In Orgrimmar, Belgrom Rockmaul calls the Gordunni ogres the dominant military force in Feralas, and their numbers are growing. They must be stopped before they threaten the Horde's presence there, and he sends the willing to the warrior Rok Orhan at Camp Mojache. Rok Orhan has seen what the ogres do: their very presence scars the land, and she means to push them back before they spread further into the forest, beginning with their outpost up the river to the north. A soiled scroll from that outpost raises a darker question, for it seems to depict some sort of meeting or ceremony of the Gordunni.
sources: quests 2981, 2975, 2980, 2978, 2979, 3002 descriptions and reward texts
notes: Converted: the opening is the premise of all three entry points (2981, 2975, 2978); the outpost cleared and the High Wilderness moved to part 1 (DONE 2975, ACCEPT 2980), the dark ceremony of the mage-lords to part 2 (ACCEPT 2979), the orb and Uthel'nay's verdict to part 3 (DONE 3002). Earlier: 2981 starts with Belgrom in Orgrimmar; 2978 starts from the Gordunni Scroll item. Fact-check: 3002 wording: she cannot tell what the orb can do.

parts.body: The ogres, brutes and ogre magi of the outpost were cut down, and Rok Orhan believes that in time the land will heal. The fight then moved southwest to the High Wilderness, where stronger shamans, warlocks and maulers hold old night elf ruins amid withered trees and desecrated ground.

parts.body: Rok Orhan read the scroll as the plans for a dark ceremony, a ritual conducted by the Gordunni mage-lords. She sought one of their orbs, sure that the orb of a mage holds power enough to reveal more of the ceremony and of the magic the ogres wield.

parts.body: An orb was taken from a mage-lord, but Rok Orhan, a warrior who knows her enemy well, could not tell what it was capable of. She sent it to the mage Uthel'nay in the Darkbriar Lodge of Orgrimmar, who found it fascinating: very powerful, and very dangerous.

title: The Muisek
body: Witch Doctor Uzer'i, a troll of Camp Mojache, teaches that incredible power can be found in the muisek, the spirits of the creatures one battles against, and he means to harness that power for the Horde. To prepare a vessel for the work, he needs herbs from an orc named Fireblade, mixed to his order and paid for with a shrunken head taken from some poor dwarf he came across in the forest. For the endeavor that is to follow he gathers natural materials as well: splintered logs from the treants of Feralas, minerals crusted on mountain giants and faerie dragons, resilient sinew from owlbeasts or hippogryphs, and a great many metallic fragments.

parts.body: The herbs prepared the vessel, and a first test proved both the ritual and the hunter: the fallen were shrunk and captured before their spirits could escape. Upon a violent death, Uzer'i explained, the muisek of a creature may flee to seek revenge, but once captured it can be used as he pleases. Then he turned the vessel on the allies of the night elves, beginning with the hippogryphs, whose spirits are loyal and steadfast.

parts.body: A muisek allowed to escape, Uzer'i warned, might take the form of an even greater creature, and no one would be safe from its vengeance, yet the work went on. Faerie dragons followed, fragile in body but strong in spirit; then the wandering treants the night elves have enlisted as protectors against the Horde; and last the mountain giants, who came down from their peaks to aid the night elves when the Burning Legion appeared in the world.

title: Errands in Eldre'Thalas
body: Both camps of Feralas send champions into Dire Maul. Lethtendris, a blood elf mage whose brutality is matched only by her craving for magic, has fled into the Warpwood Quarter among the satyrs and woven a web to snare the magical energies of the place. Heralds in the capitals call for agents, sending the Alliance to Latronicus Moonspear and the Horde to Talo Thornhoof. A quieter search is shared by two scholars, Sage Korolusk of Camp Mojache and Scholar Runethorn of Feathermoon, who work together despite their banners. They hunt for Kariel Winthalus, an elven master who fled the ruin of Quel'Thalas with ancient artifacts, and they followed his trail across the sea to Feralas. They believe he sought sanctuary in Eldre'Thalas, alive or dead.

parts.body: Lethtendris fell in the Warpwood Quarter, and her web was carried back to Latronicus. Elves of her ilk, he said, believe themselves masters of magic and do not see that they are slaves to their own addiction. Her death saddened him, but it was necessary. He will have the web's energies released safely over a wide area and then destroy it, so that it can serve no one again.
sources: quest 7488 description and reward text

parts.body: Lethtendris fell in the Warpwood Quarter, and her web was carried back to Talo. It holds vast stores of the magic of Dire Maul, and he feared what harm might come if one so irresponsible had harnessed them. He was saddened by her death, but knew she would never have parted with the web while she lived. He will send it to more responsible students of magic, to be the new wardens of its power.
sources: quest 7489 description and reward text

parts.body: The search for Kariel Winthalus ended in disappointment. No trace of the elven master was found in the halls, and the artifacts he carried are lost. It is a shame and a tragedy, the scholars lament, for they had believed themselves on the verge of a breakthrough.
